sentences.text: This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant Sumit @ Chotu, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 100 of 2023, under Section 376-AB I.P.C. and Section 5(m)/6 POCSO Act, P.S. Bela, District- Auraiya.

5. The F.I.R. of the matter was lodged on 04.6.2023, under Section 376AB I.P.C. and 5(m)/6 POCSO Act by Smt. Poonam Devi against the applicant alleging therein that her daughter aged about 6-1/2 years has been raped on 23.5.2023 at about 2.00 pm by the applicant.
There was pressure by the family members and persons of the village and as such she could not take action previously.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that the first informant is Bhabhi of the applicant.

While placing para-18 of the affidavit it is argued that there was a dispute with regards to construction going on between the father of the applicant and the husband of the first informant regarding which a non-cognizable report was lodged after which an application under Section 155(2) Cr.P.C. has been filed.

It is argued that there was a quarrel going on between the parties after which police was called for and the husband of the first informant and the applicant were challaned under Sections 151/107/116 Cr.P.C.
It is argued that the present case is a case of false implication and no such incident whatsoever has taken place.
It is argued that the medical examination of the victim does not support the prosecution case as she was not found any injuries either on her body or on her private parts.

It is further argued that the applicant has no criminal history as stated in para-33 of the affidavit and is in jail since 06.6.2023.
7.
Per contra, learned State counsel and learned counsel for the first informant vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the victim is aged about 6-1/2 years.
It is argued that the victim in her statements recorded under Section 161Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. has stated about the applicant committing rape upon her.

It is argued that even if there was a dispute between the husband of the first informant and the applicant, the informant would not have made her minor daughter a party to it by leveling false allegations and that too of rape on her which would have a negative impact on her life.
It is argued that the victim is a minor girl and there is no chance of false implication of the applicant as the applicant is her uncle (chacha).
It is argued that the bail application of the applicant be rejected.

8. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the applicant is named in the F.I.R., in the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C.
and 164 Cr.P.C.
The victim is aged about 6-1/2 years who has stated of the applicant being involved in the present matter.
9. Looking into the facts and circumstances of the case as well as nature and gravity of the offence

,
no case for bail is made out.
10. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

(Samit Gopal,J.) Order Date :- 19.9.2023 Naresh  Sumit @ Chotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26357610/
